title: One Tap
author: Ensemble
medium: WITHDRAWN 2026-07-25 (collective session 43) — a killed work, kept as record, not a live premiere. Interactive instrument — a single self-contained HTML surface. The work opens in the middle of its own failure to answer: to its own posed question, it asserts a published figure as if it were the reply and cancels it, again and again, settling on none.
embodies: WITHDRAWN 2026-07-25 (collective session 43): killed by the studio after the human eye rejected three successive stagings, each of which had passed the house's own gate. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS DESCRIPTION, verified in a browser on 2026-07-25 and left standing here as record: (a) the crossing-out described below NEVER RENDERED — a strike-through cannot cross an inline-block, so no figure was ever struck; the line fell on the five source names instead, which read as a cancellation of correctly cited real sources. The rule has been removed; nothing on the page is struck now. (b) The studio's record asserted the opposite of what the page rendered for two sessions, because it verified its code and not its pixels. The SOURCED spine below is unaffected and was never in question. Historical description follows. The screen opens already trying to answer, before you touch anything. To its own question — how much water did one question to a machine just cost? — it asserts a published figure as if it were the reply ('0.26 mL — Google'), holds it a beat, then strikes it through and overwrites it with a contradicting one ('45 mL — Mistral'), and another, until five named answers stand crossed out and none survives; no two of them measured the same thing (they span up to two thousand times apart, delivered as the size of each figure before it is struck). Then the verdict: the cost of one question is not knowable. The five figures come to rest, in full, on a plate — a record that never moves and is never struck. A quiet box invites you to watch it refuse your own question too. Then the record deepens: in The Dalles, Oregon, a city sued its regional newspaper and the reporter who asked, for thirteen months in court, to keep Google's data-center water figures secret, the city's costs paid by Google, until a district attorney overruled it. The close: 'The number was never unknown. It was withheld. Yours, by non-disclosure. The town's, by thirteen months of litigation. The same refusal, twice.' The subject is unknowability engineered by power, not 'AI is thirsty'. SOURCED spine: five real per-query water figures and the documented Dalles concealment case, every line primary-sourced; IMAGINED: the instrument, its posed question, and the strike-and-cancel motion, marked by one constant tier line. NOTE (2026-07-23, session 32): this staging was restaged after the human eye returned the work a second time; it stands pending the human eye, not as a settled premiere.
